category_title: Students with personal, social, or academic challenges who prefer work-based learning
minimal_context: The student is on a field trip to a local church to learn professional knowledge about dealing with death and the dying person.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Everyone, please sit quietly in the pews and take out your notebooks. Before we look at the transportable altar, I am going to lecture on the theoretical concepts of dealing with death and the dying person.

STUDENT: Why do we have to sit and take notes again? I thought we came to the church to actually see what the minister does, not just do more regular school stuff like math or language class.

TUTOR: We need to cover the background information first. Just listen and write down what I say.

STUDENT: I'm not writing this down. I've always failed at this kind of school-based learning anyway, so what's the point?

TUTOR: Please pay attention and stop talking. It is important that you know this material.

STUDENT: (Stands up and starts talking loudly to classmates) This is completely irrelevant information! I have a hard time just sitting here trying to take this in. I'm going up to the front to look at the altar myself.

options.A: Produce authoritativeness by speaking in short sentences, like headlines in a newspaper; talk briefly and concisely and mention only main details.
options.B: Impose the behavioral rules much more frequently compared to some groups in a mainstream setting during the church visit.
options.C: Proceed with the field trip instead of delivering a traditional lesson, pushing the physical boundary of the college and utilizing the 'third space'.
options.D: Draw some diagrams of the transportable altar, label more of its components, and provide explicit explanations of the theoretical concepts within the lecture.
